# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a

  kept region through the same repairer.

  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak and re-arms on the same
  resets), so a held gate no longer appends per-tick `wake_attempted`
  rows (~43k duplicate lines/day) and a repeat episode after user input
  is announced and receipted again. The app host receipts its wake path
  (`wake_attempted` / `turn_started` / `wake_refused`) onto the same
  trail — AC4 is no longer CLI-only. A self-reminder adopted across a
  session-id change delivers FROM the live mailbox (from re-addressed
  alongside to), so the resumed chain stays self-shaped and exempt
  instead of falling back to the capped chatter lane. Plugin-only
  pending batches are explicitly classified as chatter (the contract is

Zero false positives on real work." A bounded sleep IS arguably real work (pi-style `sleep N` between polls with a hard cap). But the tool's own max... hmm, there's no default timeout for bash. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1355
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1355
- **Title**: fix(1349): deny bare long foreground sleeps; enrich liveness reminders with the background hint
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1349-dev-agent-parks-child` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +209
- **Deletions**: -42
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T22:01:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T01:45:55Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

The harness DETECTED a long foreground call (the ⏳ running-Ns liveness notices, gh-1055) but never acted: a bare `sleep 300` foreground pinned the tool call open for minutes — owner steering cannot reach the agent, the cancel path is blocked, the runner slot burns — while the periodic notices printed 60s…120s…180s. The background escape-hatch hint only fired at the 300s escalation (gh-1055 AC3), so the incident's 230s `sleep 300` never saw it. A warned parked turn is still a parked turn.

## Fix (deny-first, convert-later per the issue's design review)

1. **Validation deny** (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart`): a BARE foreground `sleep` over 60s is rejected at call validation with the instructive message — use `background: true` + `bash_job` (action: output); background jobs notify on settle, never poll in the foreground. GNU suffixes are measured (`sleep 2m` = 120s). Deliberately conservative: sleeps wrapped in shell constructs (`sleep 300 && …`) are NOT denied — phase 2 is extend-detection, only if the deny data shows the class survives. Zero false positives on real work.
2. **Enriched ⏳ notice** (`lib/src/cli/tool_liveness.dart`): every periodic reminder line now carries `· consider background: true for long waits (settle notification wakes you)` — long foreground calls keep running untouched; the one-time escalation line is unchanged.
3. Auto-convert stays phase 2, not implemented here.

## Acceptance

- `bash {command: "sleep 300"}` (foreground) → denied with the instructive message; the shell never sees the command. `sleep 60` allowed, `sleep 61`/`sleep 2m` denied (boundary covered).
- `bash {command: "sleep 300", background: true}` → runs and settles with the notification (job id + onSettled still fire).
- A long quiet legit command (`make release`) is NOT denied and its 60s-tick reminder shows the enriched notice.
- 164/164 tests green across `test/cli/tool_liveness_test.dart`, `test/cli/agent_cli_tool_liveness_test.dart`, `test/tools/builtin_tools_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_test.dart`, `test/task/msg_slo_delivery_test.dart`; `dart analyze` on the touched files reports only pre-existing infos.

## Behavior-change note

Fixtures that stood in for "a long-running call" via a bare foreground `sleep 500/900/120` now use legitimate long work (`make release` / `make docker-pull`) — the deny IS the behavior change; the liveness/nudge/yield machinery they exercise is untouched.

Cross-link: dmtools-agents#767 — the factory-layer ban becomes redundant once fa enforces this natively.

## Verification disclosure

System toolchain is unusable on this box (machine guard SIGKILLs the dart VM, exit 137). Verified with the fleet temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + shared `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`: targeted suites above only (no project-wide runs, per lane rules). One triage note: an initial run of `agent_cli_tool_liveness_test.dart` appeared hung; reproduced on pristine origin/main as a shared pub-cache lock from a concurrent lane's `pub get` (passes in ~1.4s once the lock frees), then reproduced the REAL failure with the fix applied — the old fixtures' bare `sleep 500` was being denied at validation (which is the fix working) — hence the fixture swap above. `dart format` on two files reflowed pre-existing lines (formatter version skew, same as lane #1079 observed); reverted those two and hand-wrapped the additions to keep the diff clean.



Fixes #1349

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the

  "fields": {
    "summary": "fix(1349): deny bare long foreground sleeps; enrich liveness reminders with the background hint",
    "description": "## Root cause

The harness DETECTED a long foreground call (the ⏳ running-Ns liveness notices, gh-1055) but never acted: a bare `sleep 300` foreground pinned the tool call open for minutes — owner steering cannot reach the agent, the cancel path is blocked, the runner slot burns — while the periodic notices printed 60s…120s…180s. The background escape-hatch hint only fired at the 300s escalation (gh-1055 AC3), so the incident's 230s `sleep 300` never saw it. A warned parked turn is still a parked turn.

## Fix (deny-first, convert-later per the issue's design review)

1. **Validation deny** (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart`): a BARE foreground `sleep` over 60s is rejected at call validation with the instructive message — use `background: true` + `bash_job` (action: output); background jobs notify on settle, never poll in the foreground. GNU suffixes are measured (`sleep 2m` = 120s). Deliberately conservative: sleeps wrapped in shell constructs (`sleep 300 && …`) are NOT denied — phase 2 is extend-detection, only if the deny data shows the class survives. Zero false positives on real work.
2. **Enriched ⏳ notice** (`lib/src/cli/tool_liveness.dart`): every periodic reminder line now carries `· consider background: true for long waits (settle notification wakes you)` — long foreground calls keep running untouched; the one-time escalation line is unchanged.
3. Auto-convert stays phase 2, not implemented here.

## Acceptance

- `bash {command: "sleep 300"}` (foreground) → denied with the instructive message; the shell never sees the command. `sleep 60` allowed, `sleep 61`/`sleep 2m` denied (boundary covered).
- `bash {command: "sleep 300", background: true}` → runs and settles with the notification (job id + onSettled still fire).
- A long quiet legit command (`make release`) is NOT denied and its 60s-tick reminder shows the enriched notice.
- 164/164 tests green across `test/cli/tool_liveness_test.dart`, `test/cli/agent_cli_tool_liveness_test.dart`, `test/tools/builtin_tools_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_test.dart`, `test/task/msg_slo_delivery_test.dart`; `dart analyze` on the touched files reports only pre-existing infos.

## Behavior-change note

Fixtures that stood in for "a long-running call" via a bare foreground `sleep 500/900/120` now use legitimate long work (`make release` / `make docker-pull`) — the deny IS the behavior change; the liveness/nudge/yield machinery they exercise is untouched.

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak and re-arms on the same
  resets), so a held gate no longer appends per-tick `wake_attempted`
  rows (~43k duplicate lines/day) and a repeat episode after user input
  is announced and receipted again. The app host receipts its wake path
  (`wake_attempted` / `turn_started` / `wake_refused`) onto the same
  trail — AC4 is no longer CLI-only. A self-reminder adopted across a
  session-id change delivers FROM the live mailbox (from re-addressed
  alongside to), so the resumed chain stays self-shaped and exempt
  instead of falling back to the capped chatter lane. Plugin-only
  pending batches are explicitly classified as chatter (the contract is

blocks.text:
All 164 tests pass — matches the PR's claim. 

CHANGELOG convention: release-bump PRs assemble the changelog (chore(release) commits); individual fix PRs mostly don't touch CHANGELOG.md (last non-release change was a recovered dev leg). The PR's lack of a CHANGELOG entry is consistent with convention. Drop that.

Now let me do the exhaustive re-read pass of the changed files and finalize findings. Let me re-examine the new denial code and tests once more for edge cases:

1. **`bareForegroundSleepSeconds` — huge duration values / `truncate()`**: Let me test Dart behavior for `(1e30).truncate()` quickly.

2. **`foregroundSleepDenial` ignores `timeout`** — the false-positive class: `sleep 300` + `timeout: 30` is denied although it parks only 30s; and in environments without background support, the denial's advice ("Re-run it with background: true") dead-ends into "Background execution is not supported in this environment — run the command in the foreground with an explicit timeout" — contradictory loop. Real-world scope: mobile/web sandbox shells DO support jobs per AGENTS.md (flutter_app sandbox shells run jobs as detached futures). Which envs DON'T support jobs? MemoryExecutionEnv without shell (tests), and... `canJob = jobs != null && jobs.isSupported` — jobs registry null means the bash tool has no jobs capability. In the app and CLI, jobs are wired. In hosts without the registry (embedding hosts using builtinTools(env) with no jobs), background is unsupported. So the contradiction is real but confined to registry-less embeddings. Severity: SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT? The denial could suggest "or an explicit timeout under 60s" as fallback. Hmm. Actually wait — even WITH a timeout, the deny fires regardless. So in a registry-less host, the model literally cannot sleep >60s foreground even with a timeout — it gets a contradiction loop. But is sleeping >60s ever legit work there? The design decision says no. The message being slightly over-prescriptive is a wording quality issue → SUGGESTION.

   The `timeout` interaction though: `sleep 300` with `timeout: 45` — model explicitly bounds the call. Denied anyway. The PR description says "Deliberately conservative... Zero false positives on real work." A bounded sleep IS arguably real work (pi-style `sleep N` between polls with a hard cap). But the tool's own max... hmm, there's no default timeout for bash. The model chooses timeout explicitly. I think this deserves IMPORTANT: the deny check runs before the timeout is considered, denying an explicitly-bounded call whose parked-time is capped by the user-visible timeout — a false positive by the PR's own "zero false positives" bar. Fix: skip the deny when `timeout != null` (the call self-bounds), or only deny when no timeout. That's a small, concrete, pre-merge-able improvement. I'll file IMPORTANT.

   Hmm, wait. Let me reconsider — is it really worth IMPORTANT? Verdict rules: IMPORTANT = "real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped." The timeout case: the model passes timeout: N with sleep 300; deny fires; the model sees the message telling it to use background: true; with jobs available, it backgrounds — fine, no bug, just an unnecessary denial of a legitimate pattern. Without jobs, contradiction loop (recoverable via `sleep 60` chunks). It's a behavior wart, not a bug — the primary incident class is fixed. IMPORTANT feels right (it also weakens the "zero false positives" claim in the PR description). But per verdict rules: no BLOCKING → APPROVE.

3. **Huge-value `truncate()`**: test it. If `(1e30).truncate()` throws UnsupportedError, then `sleep 1e30`-ish (e.g. `sleep 999`) crashes the execute with an unhandled error instead of a clean denial. Severity: SUGGESTION (adversarial input, no crash of process, the loop renders error result). Let me verify what actually happens.

4. **`sleep 300` with `timeout` under the threshold... covered.

5. **Case: `sleep 60.5`** — allowed (60.5 <= 60? NO — 60.5 > 60 → DENIED). Wait: `sleep 60.5` → total=60.5 → 60.5 > 60 → denied. Hmm, `sleep 60` allowed but `sleep 60.5` denied — boundary is consistent with "> 60 denied". Fine.

6. **`words.first` case-sensitivity**: `SLEEP 300` not denied — conservative, fine.

7. **`sleep -- 300`**: not denied (word `--` no match) — false negative, fine.

8. **Escalation line after escalation**: after `escalated = true`, subsequent ticks call `_onRemind(call)` → reminder line with the SHORT hint. So after 300s, the console shows reminder lines with short hint again — the fuller escalation context was one-time. Pre-existing design, unchanged. Fine.

9. **`toolLivenessForegroundHint` duplication of guidance with the escalation hint** — wording overlap fine.

10. **Reminder-line width**: hint adds ~64 chars. The line remains single-line; grep-ability preserved; detail clip 96. Line max ≈ 200 chars. Acceptable; the tracker prints to console. Fine.

11. **Test quality**: new tests assert exact strings and boundaries — good. One gap: no test for `sleep 90.5`-style fractional seconds label, no test that `sleep 300` with `timeout` behaves (would document the current deny-anyway behavior), no test for `SLEEP 300`. Minor — could note as suggestion to pin the timeout interaction in tests. Also the deny tests don't cover the `bareForegroundSleepSeconds` API directly (only through execute) — fine.

12. **The `shell_jobs_test.dart` new test**: uses two `Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero)` — mirrors existing patterns presumably. Fine.

13. **Visual test**: `tail -f /dev/null` — real command; the job gets stopped via bash_job stop. On the CI runner (linux) `tail -f /dev/null` works. It never exits on its own — if the cancel path broke, the test would time out rather than pass falsely. Same as `sleep 300` before. Fine.

14. **`agent_cli_tool_liveness_test.dart` fixture swap to `make release`**: the fake shell (PerCallGatedShell) — `make release` is just a recorded command; no real execution. Fine. BUT one consideration: liveness detail now shows `make release`; the nudge test expects `"make release"` in the nudge text. Fine.

15. **`msg_slo_delivery_test.dart`**: AC4 renamed; `make release` backgrounded by yield; `bash_job stop` stops it. The child stream is canned (MemoryExecutionEnv). Fine.

16. **Cross-host impact of the deny**: the flutter_app (AgentService) uses builtinTools → shellTool, so mobile/web get the deny too. On mobile's WasiSandboxShell, jobs run as detached futures (supported), so background: true works. On web MemoryShell — supported. OK.

17. **The deny returns success-shaped result — does the session/trajectory record it as a tool success?** Yes, as a text tool result — matches "clean note" pattern (the availability gate tombstones similarly). Fine.

18. **Backward compatibility**: behavior change by design (the PR IS the behavior change); scripts/agents relying on `sleep 300` foreground now get denied — the instructive message mitigates. This is a deliberate policy change with cross-link to dmtools-agents#767. Documented in PR. Fine.

19. **`_sleepDurationArg` allows leading zeros `007`** → 7s. Fine.

20. **`double.parse` on `1.5`** — locale issues? No, Dart parses dot decimals. GNU sleep accepts `1.5s`. Fine.

21. One more: **`words.length < 2`** — `sleep` alone → null → allowed → real shell errors "missing operand" quickly. Fine.

22. **`bareForegroundSleepSeconds('sleep 300\n')`** — trim handles trailing newline. **`'sleep 300; '`** → word `300;` → no match → null. Fine (conservative).

23. **The hint constant name**: `toolLivenessForegroundHint` vs existing `toolLivenessEscalationHint` — consistent naming. Fine.

24. Check `test/tools/builtin_tools_test.dart` context around the new tests — the fake shell: `shell.lastCommand` reset between tests? Let me read that part of the file to confirm the fake and `_text` helper. Let me read the surrounding group quickly.

25. Also check dart analyze on the changed test files (claim: only pre-existing infos).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1355
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1355
- **Title**: fix(1349): deny bare long foreground sleeps; enrich liveness reminders with the background hint
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1349-dev-agent-parks-child` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +209
- **Deletions**: -42
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T22:01:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T01:45:55Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

The harness DETECTED a long foreground call (the ⏳ running-Ns liveness notices, gh-1055) but never acted: a bare `sleep 300` foreground pinned the tool call open for minutes — owner steering cannot reach the agent, the cancel path is blocked, the runner slot burns — while the periodic notices printed 60s…120s…180s. The background escape-hatch hint only fired at the 300s escalation (gh-1055 AC3), so the incident's 230s `sleep 300` never saw it. A warned parked turn is still a parked turn.

## Fix (deny-first, convert-later per the issue's design review)

1. **Validation deny** (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart`): a BARE foreground `sleep` over 60s is rejected at call validation with the instructive message — use `background: true` + `bash_job` (action: output); background jobs notify on settle, never poll in the foreground. GNU suffixes are measured (`sleep 2m` = 120s). Deliberately conservative: sleeps wrapped in shell constructs (`sleep 300 && …`) are NOT denied — phase 2 is extend-detection, only if the deny data shows the class survives. Zero false positives on real work.
2. **Enriched ⏳ notice** (`lib/src/cli/tool_liveness.dart`): every periodic reminder line now carries `· consider background: true for long waits (settle notification wakes you)` — long foreground calls keep running untouched; the one-time escalation line is unchanged.
3. Auto-convert stays phase 2, not implemented here.

## Acceptance

- `bash {command: "sleep 300"}` (foreground) → denied with the instructive message; the shell never sees the command. `sleep 60` allowed, `sleep 61`/`sleep 2m` denied (boundary covered).
- `bash {command: "sleep 300", background: true}` → runs and settles with the notification (job id + onSettled still fire).
- A long quiet legit command (`make release`) is NOT denied and its 60s-tick reminder shows the enriched notice.
- 164/164 tests green across `test/cli/tool_liveness_test.dart`, `test/cli/agent_cli_tool_liveness_test.dart`, `test/tools/builtin_tools_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_test.dart`, `test/task/msg_slo_delivery_test.dart`; `dart analyze` on the touched files reports only pre-existing infos.

## Behavior-change note

Fixtures that stood in for "a long-running call" via a bare foreground `sleep 500/900/120` now use legitimate long work (`make release` / `make docker-pull`) — the deny IS the behavior change; the liveness/nudge/yield machinery they exercise is untouched.

Cross-link: dmtools-agents#767 — the factory-layer ban becomes redundant once fa enforces this natively.

## Verification disclosure

System toolchain is unusable on this box (machine guard SIGKILLs the dart VM, exit 137). Verified with the fleet temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + shared `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`: targeted suites above only (no project-wide runs, per lane rules). One triage note: an initial run of `agent_cli_tool_liveness_test.dart` appeared hung; reproduced on pristine origin/main as a shared pub-cache lock from a concurrent lane's `pub get` (passes in ~1.4s once the lock frees), then reproduced the REAL failure with the fix applied — the old fixtures' bare `sleep 500` was being denied at validation (which is the fix working) — hence the fixture swap above. `dart format` on two files reflowed pre-existing lines (formatter version skew, same as lane #1079 observed); reverted those two and hand-wrapped the additions to keep the diff clean.



Fixes #1349

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

    "summary": "fix(1349): deny bare long foreground sleeps; enrich liveness reminders with the background hint",
    "description": "## Root cause

The harness DETECTED a long foreground call (the ⏳ running-Ns liveness notices, gh-1055) but never acted: a bare `sleep 300` foreground pinned the tool call open for minutes — owner steering cannot reach the agent, the cancel path is blocked, the runner slot burns — while the periodic notices printed 60s…120s…180s. The background escape-hatch hint only fired at the 300s escalation (gh-1055 AC3), so the incident's 230s `sleep 300` never saw it. A warned parked turn is still a parked turn.

## Fix (deny-first, convert-later per the issue's design review)

1. **Validation deny** (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart`): a BARE foreground `sleep` over 60s is rejected at call validation with the instructive message — use `background: true` + `bash_job` (action: output); background jobs notify on settle, never poll in the foreground. GNU suffixes are measured (`sleep 2m` = 120s). Deliberately conservative: sleeps wrapped in shell constructs (`sleep 300 && …`) are NOT denied — phase 2 is extend-detection, only if the deny data shows the class survives. Zero false positives on real work.
2. **Enriched ⏳ notice** (`lib/src/cli/tool_liveness.dart`): every periodic reminder line now carries `· consider background: true for long waits (settle notification wakes you)` — long foreground calls keep running untouched; the one-time escalation line is unchanged.
3. Auto-convert stays phase 2, not implemented here.

## Acceptance

- `bash {command: "sleep 300"}` (foreground) → denied with the instructive message; the shell never sees the command. `sleep 60` allowed, `sleep 61`/`sleep 2m` denied (boundary covered).
- `bash {command: "sleep 300", background: true}` → runs and settles with the notification (job id + onSettled still fire).
- A long quiet legit command (`make release`) is NOT denied and its 60s-tick reminder shows the enriched notice.
- 164/164 tests green across `test/cli/tool_liveness_test.dart`, `test/cli/agent_cli_tool_liveness_test.dart`, `test/tools/builtin_tools_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_test.dart`, `test/task/msg_slo_delivery_test.dart`; `dart analyze` on the touched files reports only pre-existing infos.

  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the

Zero false positives on real work." A bounded sleep IS arguably real work (pi-style `sleep N` between polls with a hard cap). But the tool's own max... hmm, there's no default timeout for bash. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

{
  "key": "pr-1355",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "fix(1349): deny bare long foreground sleeps; enrich liveness reminders with the background hint",
    "description": "## Root cause

The harness DETECTED a long foreground call (the ⏳ running-Ns liveness notices, gh-1055) but never acted: a bare `sleep 300` foreground pinned the tool call open for minutes — owner steering cannot reach the agent, the cancel path is blocked, the runner slot burns — while the periodic notices printed 60s…120s…180s. The background escape-hatch hint only fired at the 300s escalation (gh-1055 AC3), so the incident's 230s `sleep 300` never saw it. A warned parked turn is still a parked turn.

## Fix (deny-first, convert-later per the issue's design review)

1. **Validation deny** (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart`): a BARE foreground `sleep` over 60s is rejected at call validation with the instructive message — use `background: true` + `bash_job` (action: output); background jobs notify on settle, never poll in the foreground. GNU suffixes are measured (`sleep 2m` = 120s). Deliberately conservative: sleeps wrapped in shell constructs (`sleep 300 && …`) are NOT denied — phase 2 is extend-detection, only if the deny data shows the class survives. Zero false positives on real work.
2. **Enriched ⏳ notice** (`lib/src/cli/tool_liveness.dart`): every periodic reminder line now carries `· consider background: true for long waits (settle notification wakes you)` — long foreground calls keep running untouched; the one-time escalation line is unchanged.
3. Auto-convert stays phase 2, not implemented here.

## Acceptance

- `bash {command: "sleep 300"}` (foreground) → denied with the instructive message; the shell never sees the command. `sleep 60` allowed, `sleep 61`/`sleep 2m` denied (boundary covered).
- `bash {command: "sleep 300", background: true}` → runs and settles with the notification (job id + onSettled still fire).
- A long quiet legit command (`make release`) is NOT denied and its 60s-tick reminder shows the enriched notice.
- 164/164 tests green across `test/cli/tool_liveness_test.dart`, `test/cli/agent_cli_tool_liveness_test.dart`, `test/tools/builtin_tools_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_test.dart`, `test/task/msg_slo_delivery_test.dart`; `dart analyze` on the touched files reports only pre-existing infos.

## Behavior-change note

Fixtures that stood in for "a long-running call" via a bare foreground `sleep 500/900/120` now use legitimate long work (`make release` / `make docker-pull`) — the deny IS the behavior change; the liveness/nudge/yield machinery they exercise is untouched.

Cross-link: dmtools-agents#767 — the factory-layer ban becomes redundant once fa enforces this natively.

# Changelog

  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the

  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak and re-arms on the same

  rows (~43k duplicate lines/day) and a repeat episode after user input

  alongside to), so the resumed chain stays self-shaped and exempt
  instead of falling back to the capped chatter lane. Plugin-only

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >

  "key": "pr-1355",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "fix(1349): deny bare long foreground sleeps; enrich liveness reminders with the background hint",
    "description": "## Root cause

The harness DETECTED a long foreground call (the ⏳ running-Ns liveness notices, gh-1055) but never acted: a bare `sleep 300` foreground pinned the tool call open for minutes — owner steering cannot reach the agent, the cancel path is blocked, the runner slot burns — while the periodic notices printed 60s…120s…180s. The background escape-hatch hint only fired at the 300s escalation (gh-1055 AC3), so the incident's 230s `sleep 300` never saw it. A warned parked turn is still a parked turn.

## Fix (deny-first, convert-later per the issue's design review)

1. **Validation deny** (`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart`): a BARE foreground `sleep` over 60s is rejected at call validation with the instructive message — use `background: true` + `bash_job` (action: output); background jobs notify on settle, never poll in the foreground. GNU suffixes are measured (`sleep 2m` = 120s). Deliberately conservative: sleeps wrapped in shell constructs (`sleep 300 && …`) are NOT denied — phase 2 is extend-detection, only if the deny data shows the class survives. Zero false positives on real work.
2. **Enriched ⏳ notice** (`lib/src/cli/tool_liveness.dart`): every periodic reminder line now carries `· consider background: true for long waits (settle notification wakes you)` — long foreground calls keep running untouched; the one-time escalation line is unchanged.
3. Auto-convert stays phase 2, not implemented here.

## Acceptance

- `bash {command: "sleep 300"}` (foreground) → denied with the instructive message; the shell never sees the command. `sleep 60` allowed, `sleep 61`/`sleep 2m` denied (boundary covered).
- `bash {command: "sleep 300", background: true}` → runs and settles with the notification (job id + onSettled still fire).
- A long quiet legit command (`make release`) is NOT denied and its 60s-tick reminder shows the enriched notice.
- 164/164 tests green across `test/cli/tool_liveness_test.dart`, `test/cli/agent_cli_tool_liveness_test.dart`, `test/tools/builtin_tools_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_test.dart`, `test/task/msg_slo_delivery_test.dart`; `dart analyze` on the touched files reports only pre-existing infos.

## Behavior-change note

Fixtures that stood in for "a long-running call" via a bare foreground `sleep 500/900/120` now use legitimate long work (`make release` / `make docker-pull`) — the deny IS the behavior change; the liveness/nudge/yield machinery they exercise is untouched.

Cross-link: dmtools-agents#767 — the factory-layer ban becomes redundant once fa enforces this natively.

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak and re-arms on the same
  resets), so a held gate no longer appends per-tick `wake_attempted`
  rows (~43k duplicate lines/day) and a repeat episode after user input
  is announced and receipted again. The app host receipts its wake path
  (`wake_attempted` / `turn_started` / `wake_refused`) onto the same
  trail — AC4 is no longer CLI-only. A self-reminder adopted across a
  session-id change delivers FROM the live mailbox (from re-addressed
  alongside to), so the resumed chain stays self-shaped and exempt
  instead of falling back to the capped chatter lane. Plugin-only
  pending batches are explicitly classified as chatter (the contract is

Real-world scope: mobile/web sandbox shells DO support jobs per AGENTS.md (flutter_app sandbox shells run jobs as detached futures). Which envs DON'T support jobs? MemoryExecutionEnv without shell (tests), and... `canJob = jobs != null && jobs.isSupported` — jobs registry null means the bash tool has no jobs capability. In the app and CLI, jobs are wired. In hosts without the registry (embedding hosts using builtinTools(env) with no jobs), background is unsupported. So the contradiction is real but confined to registry-less embeddings. Severity: SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT? The denial could suggest "or an explicit timeout under 60s" as fallback. Hmm. Actually wait — even WITH a timeout, the deny fires regardless. So in a registry-less host, the model literally cannot sleep >60s foreground even with a timeout — it gets a contradiction loop. But is sleeping >60s ever legit work there? The design decision says no. The message being slightly over-prescriptive is a wording quality issue → SUGGESTION.

   The `timeout` interaction though: `sleep 300` with `timeout: 45` — model explicitly bounds the call. Denied anyway. The PR description says "Deliberately conservative... Zero false positives on real work." A bounded sleep IS arguably real work (pi-style `sleep N` between polls with a hard cap). But the tool's own max... hmm, there's no default timeout for bash. The model chooses timeout explicitly. I think this deserves IMPORTANT: the deny check runs before the timeout is considered, denying an explicitly-bounded call whose parked-time is capped by the user-visible timeout — a false positive by the PR's own "zero false positives" bar. Fix: skip the deny when `timeout != null` (the call self-bounds), or only deny when no timeout. That's a small, concrete, pre-merge-able improvement. I'll file IMPORTANT.

The timeout case: the model passes timeout: N with sleep 300; deny fires; the model sees the message telling it to use background: true; with jobs available, it backgrounds — fine, no bug, just an unnecessary denial of a legitimate pattern. Without jobs, contradiction loop (recoverable via `sleep 60` chunks). It's a behavior wart, not a bug — the primary incident class is fixed. IMPORTANT feels right (it also weakens the "zero false positives" claim in the PR description). But per verdict rules: no BLOCKING → APPROVE.

5. **Case: `sleep 60.5`** — allowed (60.5 <= 60? NO — 60.5 > 60 → DENIED). Wait: `sleep 60.5` → total=60.5 → 60.5 > 60 → denied. Hmm, `sleep 60` allowed but `sleep 60.5` denied — boundary is consistent with "> 60 denied". Fine.

6. **`words.first` case-sensitivity**: `SLEEP 300` not denied — conservative, fine.

12. **The `shell_jobs_test.dart` new test**: uses two `Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero)` — mirrors existing patterns presumably. Fine.

13. **Visual test**: `tail -f /dev/null` — real command; the job gets stopped via bash_job stop. On the CI runner (linux) `tail -f /dev/null` works. It never exits on its own — if the cancel path broke, the test would time out rather than pass falsely. Same as `sleep 300` before. Fine.

BUT one consideration: liveness detail now shows `make release`; the nudge test expects `"make release"` in the nudge text. Fine.

18. **Backward compatibility**: behavior change by design (the PR IS the behavior change); scripts/agents relying on `sleep 300` foreground now get denied — the instructive message mitigates. This is a deliberate policy change with cross-link to dmtools-agents#767. Documented in PR. Fine.

21. One more: **`words.length < 2`** — `sleep` alone → null → allowed → real shell errors "missing operand" quickly. Fine.

22. **`bareForegroundSleepSeconds('sleep 300\n')`** — trim handles trailing newline. **`'sleep 300; '`** → word `300;` → no match → null. Fine (conservative).

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
